Subject: Governance exceptions for local SI deployments (EU & APAC)

Team —

Following the calls with ZenConsult and NovaTech this week, they asked for a documented exception flow for a couple of data-residency constraints when we run Redwood Private through their on-prem / VPC-managed delivery. High level asks:

- ZenConsult (JP/EU) needs a documented path for a temporary audit-exception when a customer requires a local SI to manage keys for an initial POC (3–6 months).
- NovaTech (CN/SG) is requesting a narrow exception: allow ephemeral customer-owned key-mirroring into a partner-controlled HSM during a pilot, with strict logging and automated expiry.

I want us to capture an operational "governance exception" playbook that:
1) defines the decision authority (who approves: legal + security + regional director),
2) lists the minimum controls required (KMS/HSM attestation, audit log retention, read-only access policies, journey to full private deployment), and
3) defines timeline and rollback triggers.

Attached are the initial notes they shared and a rough deployment map from their engineering teams. Please review and flag the hard blockers. We need a proposed owner and a recommended SLO for approval decision within 48 hours — we have a follow-up sync with both SIs on Friday.

Attachments: si-deployment-map-apac-eu.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
T: +1 415-555-0147

From: Satoshi Ito <satoshi@zenconsulti.jp>

Subject: Re: Governance exceptions for local SI deployments (EU & APAC)

Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick summary and for pulling the team together. A few clarifications from our end:

1) The customer in Germany will not accept cross-border key control during the POC; ZenConsult is willing to manage keys locally but requires a documented exception from Redwood that outlines the controls and the maximum duration (we proposed 90 days).

2) We can provide HSM attestation reports and a technical runbook for how the keys are generated, rotated, and purged. We will not have access to application-layer logs — only HSM operational audit logs.

3) For NovaTech's pilot: they need automated expiry and a webhook to verify key state changes back to the customer's security team (they will act as the data controller).

We are fine with a conservative approach: short-duration exceptions, mandatory attestation, and a formal sign-off before any pilot starts. Can you confirm who at Redwood signs that sign-off (legal + security contact names)?

Best,
Satoshi Ito
Head of Strategic Systems | ZenConsult

Satoshi / Mei / Team —

Thanks for the detail. From a legal/compliance perspective I can draft a tightly-scoped exception agreement that sits on top of our standard DPA. Key points I will require before sign-off:

- Exact duration (we should aim for 60–90 days max for POC exceptions).
- A list of specific accounts/customers and their controlling PO/contract.
- HSM vendor attestation reports, and an architectural diagram showing where keys live and who can perform crypto operations.
- A documented rollback/termination trigger (e.g., failed attestation, unauthorized access event).

I'm attaching a DPA appendix template that we can tailor (dpa-draft-redwood-v1.pdf). Please note: exceptions will be executed as a signed appendix, not an untracked email approval.

Attachments: dpa-draft-redwood-v1.pdf (pdf)

Marissa Cole

All —

Operational considerations from infra/ops:

- We need a clear deployment topology for each exception: where the inference runtime is hosted, where model weights are kept, and whether KV cache or prefix caching touches customer data. The attached map helps but we need annotated network boundaries.
- Minimum controls to enforce programmatically: mutual TLS for control plane calls, HSM-backed key usage with time-limited credentials, and syslog shipping to a Redwood read-only audit bucket with 90-day retention for exceptions.
- Automations: we can provide a webhook and periodic compliance snapshot (daily heartbeat) to the customer's security team. We'll need a runbook and a named owner for the exception (ops on-call + SI lead).

Link to runbook draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSI-runbooks
